questions.question: Sports Authority of India comes under which ministry?
questions.questionHtml: Sports Authority of India comes under which ministry?

options.text: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
options.html: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare

options.text: Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
options.html: Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports.

Key Points

  • The Sports Authority of India (SAI) operates under the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports, Government of India.
  • SAI was established in 1984 to promote sports and oversee the development of sports facilities and training programs in India.
  • It is responsible for the preparation of athletes for major international events such as the Olympics, Asian Games, and Commonwealth Games.
  • SAI also manages various sports training centers and academies across the country, providing infrastructure, coaching, and other support to budding sportspersons.

Additional Information

  • Ministry of Education:
    • The Ministry of Education is responsible for the development and implementation of educational policies and programs in India.
    • It oversees various institutions such as the University Grants Commission (UGC), National Council of Educational Research and Training (NCERT), and others.
    • The Ministry's focus is on improving the quality of education and ensuring access to education for all.
  • Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment:
    • This ministry focuses on the welfare, social justice, and empowerment of disadvantaged and marginalized sections of society.
    • It implements schemes and policies for the upliftment of Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, Other Backward Classes, Divyangjan (Persons with Disabilities), and other vulnerable groups.
  • Ministry of Health and Family Welfare:
    • The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare is responsible for the formulation and implementation of health policies and programs in India.
    • It aims to ensure the accessibility and affordability of quality healthcare for all citizens.
    • It manages various national health schemes like Ayushman Bharat, National Health Mission, and others.
  • Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports:
    • The Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports is dedicated to the development and promotion of sports and youth welfare in India.
    • It formulates policies and programs to nurture young talent in sports and provides necessary infrastructure and training facilities.
    • It also organizes national and international sports events and collaborates with various sports bodies and organizations.

questions.question: Who among the following has given extraordinary powers during an emergency?
questions.questionHtml: Who among the following has given extraordinary powers during an emergency?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is The President.

Key Points

  • President of India: 
    • Under the Constitution of India, the President can declare a national emergency if the security of India is threatened by war, external aggression, or armed rebellion.
    • During a national emergency, the President has the power to suspend certain fundamental rights, suspend the operation of the Parliament, and direct the states to act according to the instructions of the central government.
    • This power has been used in response to a variety of crises, including the 1962 Sino-Indian War, the 1971 Indo-Pakistani War, and the 1975 Emergency.

Additional Information

  • Prime Minister of India:-
    • It is the head of the government of India.
    • He or she is the chief executive of the Union and the leader of the majority party in the Lok Sabha.
    • The Prime Minister is appointed by the President of India and must command the confidence of the Lok Sabha.
  • Chief Justice of India:-
    • CJI is the head of the Supreme Court of India, the highest court in the country.
    • He or she is also the head of the Indian judicial system.
    • The CJI is appointed by the President of India on the recommendation of the Prime Minister and the Collegium of Judges.
  • Governor:-
    • The Governor of a state in India is the constitutional head of the state.
    • They are appointed by the president of India and hold office for a term of five years.
    • The governor is responsible for upholding the constitution and the law in the state.

questions.question: Originally, the Constitution of India had ________ Schedules.
questions.questionHtml: <font style="vertical-align: inherit;"><font style="vertical-align: inherit;">Originally, the Constitution of India had ________ Schedules.</font></font>
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 8.

Key Points

  • The Constitution of India:
    • The Constitution of India is the supreme law of the land, laying down the framework that defines the political principles, establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.
  • Schedules in the Constitution:
    • The Constitution originally had 8 schedules, but now it has 12 schedules. These schedules are lists in the Constitution that categorize and tabulate bureaucratic activity and government policy.
  • Details of the 12 Schedules:
    • First Schedule: Lists the states and territories of India.
    • Second Schedule: Provisions related to the President, Governors, Judges, and Comptroller and Auditor General of India.
    • Third Schedule: Forms of Oaths or Affirmations.
    • Fourth Schedule: Allocation of seats in the Rajya Sabha.
    • Fifth Schedule: Provisions related to the administration and control of Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes.
    • Sixth Schedule: Provisions for the administration of tribal areas in Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram.
    • Seventh Schedule: Division of powers between the Union and States (Union List, State List, and Concurrent List).
    • Eighth Schedule: Lists the official languages recognized by the Constitution.
    • Ninth Schedule: Contains acts and laws that are exempt from judicial review.
    • Tenth Schedule: Provisions related to disqualification of members on the ground of defection.
    • Eleventh Schedule: Specifies the powers, authority, and responsibilities of Panchayats.
    • Twelfth Schedule: Specifies the powers, authority, and responsibilities of Municipalities.

    • The ministry of environment and forests notified the Ganges River Dolphin as the National Aquatic Animal in 2010.

questions.questionHtml: Who conducts elections for both the houses of Parliament in India?

  • The **Election Commission of India** is an autonomous constitutional authority responsible for administering election processes in India at both the national and state levels.
  • It ensures **free and fair elections** to the Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha, and State Legislative Assemblies, as well as the offices of the President and Vice President in the country.
  • It was established on **25th January 1950** under the Constitution of India.
  • The Commission operates under the authority of **Article 324** of the Indian Constitution.

questions.question: Who is also known as Panchayat President?
questions.questionHtml: Who is also known as Panchayat President?

Key Points

  • The grassroots level of Panchayati Raj is Gram Panchayat.
  • The gram panchayat is divided into wards and each ward is represented by ward Member known as Panchayat member.
  • The panchayat president is known as Sarpanch.

  • Each ward elects a representative who is known as the Ward Member (Panch). All the members of the Gram Sabha also elect a Sarpanch who is the Panchayat President.
  • The Gram Panchayat is elected for five years. The Gram Panchayat has a Secretary who is also the Secretary of the Gram Sabha.
  • This person is not an elected person but is appointed by the government. The Secretary is responsible for calling the meeting of the Gram Sabha and Gram Panchayat and keeping a record of the proceedings

questions.question: A compilation of norms and guidelines to be followed by political parties and contesting candidates at the time of election is called ________.
questions.questionHtml: A compilation of norms and guidelines to be followed by political parties and contesting candidates at the time of election is called ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is code of conduct.

Important Points

  • A compilation of norms and guidelines to be followed by political parties and contesting candidates at the time of election is called code of conduct.
  • Code of Conduct is a set of norms and guidelines to be followed by the political parties and contesting candidates during election time.
  • The Election Commission of India issues a set of guidelines for candidates and political parties to follow during elections.
  • Speeches, polling booths, polling day conduct, election manifestos, processions, and general conduct are all covered under the criteria.
  • It comes into effect as soon as the election schedule is announced by the Election Commission of India.
  • Respective parties are required to notify the local police department in advance of scheduled meetings, providing accurate information on the location and time, in order to maintain law and order and control traffic in the area.
  • During the election process, government bodies are barred from participating in any recruitment procedure.
  • Kerala was the first state in India to use the model code of conduct in its elections in 1960.

questions.question: When several political parties join hands to form a government and exercise political power on the basis of a consensus programme agenda, it is called what?
questions.questionHtml: <font style="vertical-align: inherit;"><font style="vertical-align: inherit;">When several political parties join hands to form a government and exercise political power on the basis of a consensus programme agenda, it is called what?  </font></font>

options.html: <font style="vertical-align: inherit;"><font style="vertical-align: inherit;">Majority party government</font></font>

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Coalition government.

Key Points

  • A coalition government is formed when multiple political parties join hands to create a majority in the legislature.
  • This type of government usually arises when no single party gains a sufficient number of seats to form a majority on its own.
  • Coalition governments are based on a consensus programme agenda agreed upon by all the participating parties.
  • Such a government requires constant negotiation and compromise among the member parties to maintain stability.
  • Examples include the Indian National Democratic Alliance (NDA) and the United Progressive Alliance (UPA).

Additional Information

  • Majority Party Government
    • A majority party government is when a single political party wins more than half the seats in the legislature and forms the government independently.
    • It usually results in a more stable and efficient administration as compared to coalition governments.
  • Presidential Government
    • This system features a president who serves as both the head of state and the head of government.
    • It is characterized by a clear separation of powers between the executive and the legislature.
    • Examples include the United States and Brazil.
  • One-Party System
    • In a one-party system, a single political party controls the government and other parties are either banned or allowed limited participation.
    • It often leads to a lack of political pluralism and can be associated with authoritarian regimes.
    • Examples include China and North Korea.
  • Consensus Programme Agenda
    • This refers to an agreed-upon set of policies and priorities that coalition parties commit to implementing together.
    • It ensures that all coalition members have a stake in the government’s agenda, promoting cooperation and reducing conflicts.

    • He is a retired judge of the Supreme Court of India.
    • On 28 May 2022,Shri Justice Pradip Kumar Mohanty was appointed as the acting Chairperson of the Lokpal after the superannuation of the first Lokpal chairperson Pinaki Chandra Ghose.

Important Points

  • A Lokpal is an anti-corruption authority or body of ombudsman who represents the public interest in the Republic of India.

  • The Lokpal consists of a Chairperson and eight members. Four of the judicial members have been former Chief Justices of different High Courts and the four non-judicial members have been from All India Services/Central Services.

questions.question: Subsidies are provided by the government keeping in mind the ______ of public.
questions.questionHtml: Subsidies are provided by the government keeping in mind the ______ of public.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is welfare.

Key Points

  •  Subsidies:-
    • Subsidies are provided by the government keeping in mind the welfare of the public.
    • The goal of subsidies is to make essential goods and services more affordable and accessible for everyone, especially those who are low-income or struggling financially.
    • Subsidies can also be used to promote certain economic or social goals, such as supporting domestic industries, encouraging innovation, or reducing environmental pollution.
    • Examples of how subsidies can benefit the public:
      • Food subsidies: Food subsidies can help to reduce the cost of food for low-income families and ensure that everyone has access to nutritious food.
      • Education subsidies: Education subsidies can make education more affordable for students and families, and help to promote educational equality.
      • Healthcare subsidies: Healthcare subsidies can make healthcare more affordable for people who are uninsured or underinsured, and help to improve access to quality healthcare.
      • Housing subsidies: Housing subsidies can help low-income families to afford safe and decent housing.
      • Energy subsidies: Energy subsidies can help to reduce the cost of energy for low-income households and businesses, and can also be used to promote renewable energy sources.

questions.question: Which Amendment Act of Indian Constitution gave constitutional status to Panchayati Raj System?
questions.questionHtml: Which Amendment Act of Indian Constitution gave constitutional status to Panchayati Raj System?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 3 i.e 73rd.

  • The idea of the Panchayati Raj system in India signifies the system of rural local self-government.
    • The 73rd amendment act of the Indian constitution gave constitutional status to the Panchayati raj system.
    • The 73rd amendment act added a new part IX and Articles 243 to 243 O to the Indian constitution.
    • The 73rd amendment act added the eleventh schedule to the Indian constitution.
    • The term Panchayati raj was coined by Jawahar lal Nehru.
    • Panchayati Raj Act came into force on 24th April 1993.
    • April 24th is observed as the national Panchayati raj day since 2011.
  • Important committees constituted for recommendations regarding Panchayati raj in India:
    • Balwant Rai Mehta committee.
    • V.T. Krishnammachari committee.
    • Ashok Mehta Committee.
    • G.V.K. Rao Committee.
    • L.M. Singhvi Committee.
    • P.K. Thungon Committee.
  • ​The 71st amendment included Konkani, Manipuri, and Nepali languages in the eighth schedule.
  • ​The 72nd amendment provided reservations to scheduled tribes in Tripura state legislative assembly.
  • The 74th amendment act gave constitutional status to the municipalities.

questions.question: The Union List or State List is given in which schedule of constitution of India?
questions.questionHtml: The Union List or State List is given in which schedule of constitution of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 3 i.e., Seventh Schedule

  • The Seventh Schedule of the Constitution of India defines and specifies the allocation of powers and functions between States and the Union.
  • The schedule contains three lists - Union List, State List, and Concurrent list.
    • The Union List originally had 97 subjects. Now, it has 100 subjects. The centre has exclusive powers to make laws on the subjects mentioned in this list.
    • The State List has 61 subjects now, It had 66 subjects initially. State legislatures can make laws on the subjects mentioned in this list.
    • The Concurrent List has 52 subjects enumerated under it. Both the State as well as the Central Government can make laws mentioned on this list.
Schedule Description
Fourth Allocation of seats in the Rajya Sabha to the States and the Union Territories.
Sixth Provisions relating to the administration of the tribal areas in the states of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram.
Ninth It consists of a list of Central and state laws that cannot be challenged in courts.

questions.question: Which of the following is the first official language of Sri Lanka?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following is the first official language of Sri Lanka?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Sinhala.

Key Points

  • One of the official languages of Sri Lanka is Sinhalese.
  • It's the Sinhalese people's native language, who total approximately 16 million.
  • A further 4 million speak Sinhalese as a second language.
  • This language belongs to the Indo-European family.
  • Within that category, is a component of the Indo-Aryan branch.
  • It's written with the Sinhalese alphabet which descends from the ancient Indian Brahmi writing.
  • Modern-Sinhalese is traced to the Dravidian as well as Pali and the medieval version of Sinhalese.
  • it's also borrowed words from Tamil, Portuguese, Dutch, and English.
  • The Rodiya community within Sri Lanka speaks a dialect of Sinhalese called Rodiya.
  • it's considered an indication of belonging to a lower-caste in the society.

Additional Information

  • English:
    • It is the official language of Arunachal Pradesh.
    • It is not included in the schedule 8 of the Indian constitution.
  • Malayalam:
    • It is the official language of Kerala.
    • It is derived from Sanskrit language.
  • Tamil:
    • It is the official language of Tamil Nadu.
    • It is included in the Schedule 8 of the Indian Constitution.

questions.question: In which amendment to the constitution were the Bodo, Dogri, Santhali and Maithli added to the list of recognised languages?
questions.questionHtml: In which amendment to the constitution were the Bodo, Dogri, Santhali and Maithli added to the list of recognised languages?
questions.solution: The 92nd Amendment Act of 2003 added Bodo, Dogri, Maithili, and Santhali to the list of recognized languages in the Indian Constitution. The Sindhi language was included by the 21st Amendment Act of 1967, while Konkani, Manipuri, and Nepali were added by the 71st Amendment Act of 1992. Articles 343 to 351 in Part XVII of the Indian Constitution address official languages. The 73rd Amendment Act of 1992 established the three-tier Panchayati Raj system, the 101st Amendment Act of 2016 implemented GST, and the 103rd Amendment Act of 2019 provided a 10% reservation for the economically weaker sections.

questions.question: On which day was the National Emblem of India adopted?
questions.questionHtml: On which day was the National Emblem of India adopted?
questions.solution: The National Emblem of India was adopted on 26th January 1950. It is based on the Lion Capital of Ashoka at Sarnath, Uttar Pradesh, and its motto is 'Satyamev Jayate' meaning 'Truth Alone Triumphs.' The emblem is a symbol of power and is used in all official government communications. Its use is governed by the State Emblem of India (Prohibition of Improper Use) Act-2005. It can be displayed in key public buildings such as Rashtrapati Bhawan, Parliament House, Supreme Court, and other significant government structures and diplomatic missions. Unauthorized use of the emblem is illegal.

questions.question: The ______ Amendment of the Constitution of India envisages the Gram Sabha as the foundation of the Panchayat Raj System to perform functions and powers entrusted to it by the State Legislatures.
questions.questionHtml: The ______ Amendment of the Constitution of India envisages the Gram Sabha as the foundation of the Panchayat Raj System to perform functions and powers entrusted to it by the State Legislatures.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 73rd.

Key Points

  • The 73rd Amendment of the Constitution of India envisages the Gram Sabha as the foundation of the Panchayat Raj System to perform functions and powers entrusted to it by the State Legislatures.
  • The Constitution (73rd Amendment) Act, 1992 has added a new part IX consisting of 16 Articles and the Eleventh Schedule to the Constitution.
  • The 73rd Amendment envisages the Gram Sabha as the foundation of the Panchayat Raj System to perform functions and powers entrusted to it by the State Legislatures.

Additional Information

  • The amendment provides for a three-tier Panchayat Raj System at the village, intermediate, and district levels. 
  • Articles 243A provides that the Gram Sabha may exercise such power and perform such functions at the village level as the Legislature of a State may by law provide.
  • The eleventh schedule of the constitution created by the 73rd Amendment contains 29 subjects on which the Panchayats shall have administrative control, Articles 243H empowers State Legislature to make provisions for imposing taxes, etc. by the panchayat.

  • Thus, we can conclude that the 73rd Amendment of the Constitution of India, is related to Panchayats.

questions.question: The Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner, India comes under the:
questions.questionHtml: The Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner, India comes under the:
questions.solution: The Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner, India, functions under the Ministry of Home Affairs. This office is tasked with conducting the decennial Census of India and compiling vital statistics on population metrics such as birth and death rates. The data collected is essential for governmental planning, policy-making, resource allocation, and the implementation of welfare programs. The Ministry of Home Affairs handles internal security, border management, Union Territories administration, disaster management, and oversees the Central Armed Police Forces and the official languages policy. The Registrar General's office was established in 1949 and conducts the Census every ten years.

questions.question: The State emblem of India is an adaptation of the:
questions.questionHtml: The State emblem of India is an adaptation of the:

options.text: Lion Capital of Asoka at Sarnath
options.html: Lion Capital of Asoka at Sarnath

options.text: Allahabad Stone Pillar Inscription of Samudra Gupta
options.html: Allahabad Stone Pillar Inscription of Samudra Gupta

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Lion Capital of Asoka at Sarnath.

Key Points 

  • The State Emblem of India is an adaptation of the lion capital of Asoka at Sarnath.
  • The state emblem of India consists of four lions, standing back to back.
    • Among the four lions, only three lions are visible, the fourth being hidden from view. 
    • The mouths of lions are open roaring or spreading the dharma.
  • The state emblem of India consists of a drum on which four animals are carved representing the four cardinal directions:
    • A horse (west).
    • An ox (east).
    • An elephant (south).
    • A lion (north).
  • The capital is crowned by the wheel of the law (Dharma Chakra).
  • The state emblem of India was adopted on 26th January 1950.
  • The word Satyameva Jayate is inscribed below the abacus in Devanagari script.

Additional Information 

  • Vaishali is a district in Bihar, 
    • The Vaishali pillar has only a single lion capital.
  • Sanchi stupa is a Buddhist complex in Madhya Pradesh.
    • it was built by Emperor Ashoka in the 3rd century BC.
  • The Allahabad pillar inscription was originally installed by Asoka at Kausambi.
    • It was shifted to Allahabad Fort.
    • It contains three inscriptions belonging to the time of Asoka, Samudragupta, and Jahangir.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct with respect to the political parties in India?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following statements is correct with respect to the political parties in India?

options.text: A political party symbol is assigned by the President of India.
options.html: A political party symbol is assigned by the President of India.

options.text: India has a multi-party system classified as national, state or regional level.
options.html: India has a multi-party system classified as national, state or regional level.

options.text: All parties are registered with the Supreme Court of India.
options.html: All parties are registered with the Supreme Court of India.

options.text: Status of party is accorded by the Parliament.
options.html: Status of party is accorded by the Parliament.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is India has a multi-party system classified as national, state or regional level..

Key Points

  • India follows a multi-party system where multiple political parties can exist and participate in elections.
  • Political parties in India are classified into national, state or regional level based on their performance and influence.
  • National parties are those that have influence over a larger part of India, while state or regional parties have influence limited to specific states or regions.
  • This classification helps in managing the democratic process and ensuring representation at both the national and state levels.

Additional Information

  • Election Commission of India (ECI)
    • The Election Commission of India is an autonomous constitutional authority responsible for administering election processes in India at both the national and state levels.
    • It administers elections to the Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha, and State Legislative Assemblies, as well as the offices of the President and Vice President in the country.
    • The ECI ensures free and fair elections in India.
  • Registration of Political Parties
    • Political parties in India are registered with the Election Commission of India under the Representation of the People Act, 1951.
    • Registration with the ECI is a precondition for a political party to be recognized as a national or state party.
  • Recognition of Political Parties
    • The status of a political party, whether national or state, is determined based on its performance in elections.
    • Criteria for recognition include the number of seats won in elections and the percentage of votes obtained.
  • Symbols of Political Parties
    • The Election Commission of India assigns symbols to political parties to help voters identify them during elections.
    • Symbols play a significant role in the election process, especially for illiterate voters who may not recognize party names.
